request.spec:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the
tree receives the next number after the last number given anywhere in the tree (numbers given before
this stay as they are). Per-period numbering stays per sheet.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheets of a tree now share one sheet-wide number sequence: a claim opened on any sheet of the
tree receives the next number after the last number given anywhere in the tree (numbers given before
this stay as they are). Per-period numbering stays per sheet.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims opened on any sheet of a tree now take the next number after the last one given anywhere in that tree. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The change is on the server only and needed no database migration. Each sheet already records the last number it gave out, so nothing new had to be stored.

- **`SheetService.nextClaimNumber`:** it now finds the tree by following parents up to the top sheet, then collecting every sheet below it. It locks each sheet in the tree, takes the highest last number among them, and gives the opened claim the next one.
- **Existing numbers:** numbers already given are left as they are; only new claims use the shared count.
- **Per-period numbers:** these (like `P1-1`) are unchanged. They still count per sheet and don't advance the shared count.
- **`Sheet`:** I added a way to read a sheet's last number and to take the next one after a given number. I removed the old method that only counted within one sheet, since nothing else called it.

One thing to know: opening a claim on one sheet briefly locks every sheet in its tree. That stops two people on different sheets of the same tree getting the same number at the same moment, but it means those openings wait for each other.
